tutorial-packkeeper-title: A note from Bram Alder, the Packkeeper
tutorial-packkeeper-byline: For the handler who has just acquired an animal with opinions
tutorial-packkeeper-intro: Your companion is clever enough to have opinions, and stubborn enough to keep them. Here is how to give those opinions somewhere useful to go.
tutorial-start-text: With an empty hand, right-click an owned companion to open this journal. Holding an item keeps that item's normal interaction available. The question-mark button opens these instructions again.
tutorial-activity-text: Follow keeps the companion near you. At Ease permits wandering, socializing, play, and ordinary rest. Rest sends it to recover at its assigned den. Return Home knows the way home no matter the distance, heading for its den or Pack Cart and using a safe fallback if the route fails.
tutorial-combat-text: Combat style decides when the companion fights. Risk tolerance decides when it retreats: Cautious heads home below 40% health, Steady below 20%, and Fearless never retreats automatically. Passive never fights. Defensive fights back. Protect and Assist help you. Aggressive looks for trouble. Flee avoids it.
tutorial-progress-text: Check in for requests and companion points. Talents improve an individual companion. Pack status shows the wider roster. The Pack Cart handles shared cargo, recruitment, and expeditions.
tutorial-packkeeper-last-word: Do not worry if the animal ignores you at first. It is probably thinking. If it is not thinking, check whether you told it to Follow.
tutorial-packkeeper-reminder: Bram Alder's instructions can always be reopened with the ? button in any Companion window.
help-companion-start-text: With an empty hand, right-click your tamed animal to open this screen. Holding an item keeps that item's normal interaction available.
help-companion-requests-text: Check in asks for one contextual request. A normal completion awards one companion point and one shared pack point. Timed requests must stay satisfied continuously; Cancel abandons the request and starts its cooldown.
help-companion-activity-text: Follow travels with you and suppresses ordinary wandering. At Ease permits normal pack life. Rest walks to the assigned den. Return Home knows the way home regardless of distance and may safely teleport only as a fallback.
help-companion-combat-text: Combat style controls when the companion fights. Cautious retreats home below 40% health, Steady below 20%, and Fearless never retreats automatically. Companions never attack players.
help-companion-wounded-text: A mortally wounded companion cannot open this screen. Hold Ctrl and use a compatible healing item to begin recovery.
help-companion-pack-text: Pack status opens the shared roster and cache; the Pack Cart manages routes and expeditions. Carried Collection Box cargo remains secured on the companion until delivery or manual retrieval.
help-companion-personality-text: Personality changes voice, request preferences, and pack-life choices—not combat or expedition statistics.
help-pack-roster-text: Roster shows every active companion's species, health, mood, personality, points, cargo, and availability. Dead companions remain there until archived; Archived preserves their identity and history.
help-pack-cart-active-text: This is the active Pack Cart. Select mixed-species parties, unlock routes, prepare journeys, begin expeditions, and review saved field reports here.
help-pack-cart-status-text: This view provides roster, cache, and archive access. Use your active Pack Cart to select parties, unlock routes, prepare journeys, and begin expeditions.
help-pack-routes-text: Pack points are shared. Route purchases are permanent; expedition preparation spends points once to reduce that journey's danger. Companion points remain personal and buy talents.
help-pack-cache-text: Cargo and queued recruitment results are saved in the cart cache until claimed, and block new departures while any reward remains. Nearby companions can deliver item cargo to a Pack Collection Box. Recruitment companions are claimed one at a time.
help-pack-reports-text: Reports opens the saved expedition history; Open exact ledger shows every recorded companion, talent, strength value, and cargo stack. Dining, resting, play, and lookout landmarks are communal—not personal assignments.
help-pack-scroll-note: Use the mouse wheel over long rosters, cargo lists, parties, or ledgers to scroll.
help-storage-target-text: Hold the Pack Ledger and right-click a storage block that exposes a writable item inventory. The ledger shows the block it is configuring. Ordinary modded containers work automatically; output-only and liquid-processing inventories are excluded unless a mod explicitly opts them in.
help-storage-category-text: Select one or more categories for this container. Advanced mode imports exact collectible types from items in the container; click a type to allow or exclude it. In category mode, General is the catch-all destination. Use Remove to clear this destination's rules.
help-storage-priority-text: Foxes prefer the fullest matching single-category container, then a matching container configured for several categories, then General. Distance is only the final tie-breaker between otherwise equal choices. Full or incompatible containers are skipped.
help-storage-general-text: Pack Collection Boxes begin as General storage. General is the lowest-priority fallback, so it is a good emergency drop-off without competing with a purpose-set container. A companion's Duties tab can also allow sorting matching items out of General later.
help-storage-food-text: Food includes anything the player can eat or drink, including modded food and wine. Boulders are not a category because they break into ordinary rocks, which are Stone.
help-talent-points-text: Talent points belong to this companion and are earned by completing normal requests.
help-talent-branches-text: Combat improves resilience and future fighting power. Survival covers movement, hazards, awareness, and recovery. Social covers requests, pack actions, and specializations.
help-talent-rank-text: Rank up spends the displayed cost. A locked card names the first unmet tree gate, prerequisite, exclusive choice, or point requirement.
help-talent-respec-text: Respec refunds all points spent in this tree set. It does not remove the companion's request history or pack points.
help-talent-hover-text: Hover over a talent for its effect, use condition, current rank, tree gate, and exact availability. Green means ready, amber means testing, and red means coming later.
help-talent-saved-text: Talent ranks are saved with the companion. Points and ranks are individual, so spending points on one companion does not unlock talents on another.
guide-pack-title: A note from Bram Alder, the Packkeeper
guide-pack-byline: This is the home hub of the pack
guide-pack-text: Pack status is the home hub for the whole pack, not just the animal you clicked. Use it to see every companion, archived records, cargo in the shared cache, and pack points. The Handbook has the plain reference version.
guide-pack-cart-importance-text: When you can, make a Pack Cart one of your first priorities. It is the pack's headquarters: the place to choose expedition parties, unlock routes, prepare journeys, send companions out for work, and collect the reports and rewards they bring home.
guide-pack-cart-title: A note from Bram Alder, the Packkeeper
guide-pack-cart-byline: Congratulations. The pack has a home now.
guide-pack-cart-text: This Pack Cart is the pack's headquarters. Roster shows who belongs to the pack. Expeditions can send multiple disjoint parties and tracks each return. Routes unlock longer or more specialized journeys. Pack cache holds cargo and queued recruitment results until you claim them. Archived keeps old records. Reports remembers what happened. The Handbook has the plain reference version.
guide-talent-title: A note from Bram Alder, the Packkeeper
guide-talent-byline: Talents belong to the individual animal
guide-talent-text: Spend that companion's points to buy talents; points are not shared between animals. Combat improves resilience and fighting power. Survival covers movement, hazards, awareness, and recovery. Social / Economy covers requests, pack actions, and specializations. Ranks may require tree investment or other talents. Hover a card to see its effect, current rank, cost, requirements, and whether it is ready, being tested, or coming later. Respec refunds spent talent points. The Handbook has the plain reference version.
handbook-pack-ledger-text:
CRAFTING

Craft a Pack Ledger from one plank, one piece of charcoal, and one flax twine. Any book can replace the plank if preferred. Hold the ledger and right-click storage with a writable item inventory to configure that destination.

SUPPORTED STORAGE

Storage is detected through the standard block-inventory capability, so ordinary modded containers work without a Companions-specific patch. Output-only and liquid-processing inventories are excluded by default; a modded hybrid container can explicitly opt in with the block attribute feralKinshipStorageRouting set to include, while a machine can opt out with exclude.

GENERAL AND PRIORITY

General storage accepts anything and is the lowest-priority fallback. Advanced exact-item destinations take priority over category destinations; otherwise foxes prefer the fullest single-category destination, then a box configured for several matching categories, then General. Distance breaks ties between otherwise equal choices. If every matching specific destination is full or cannot accept the item, the fox falls back to General.

ADVANCED ITEM RULES

Choose Advanced while configuring a container that has sample items inside. It imports the exact collectible types currently in that container. Click a type to exclude it or allow it again; Add current contents imports new types without changing prior choices. Unlisted types are not accepted while Advanced mode is active. These rules match collectible types, not durability or other stack attributes; item-family grouping is not included yet. Use Categories to return to broad category routing.

General boxes can act as an unsorted drop-off: while General storage sorting is enabled in a companion's Duties overview, that companion may move stored items into matching specific boxes. Disabling it stops only this rearranging; newly collected items still follow configured routing.

FOOD

Food is intentionally broad. Anything the player can eat or drink is treated as Food when practical, including modded edible items and wine.
handbook-companion-guide-text:
COMPANION WINDOW

Open a Companion window by empty-hand right-clicking an owned companion. Use the question-mark button for the screen's detailed help.

ACTIVITY

Follow keeps the companion near the player and suppresses ordinary wandering. At Ease permits normal wandering, socializing, play, and ordinary rest. Rest sends the companion to its assigned den to recover. Return Home knows the way back regardless of distance. It walks normally first and uses teleportation only as a safe fallback.

COMBAT

Combat style controls when the companion fights: Passive never fights; Defensive fights after being attacked; Protect defends the owner and nearby owned companions; Assist joins fights started by the owner; Aggressive seeks valid hostile targets; Flee avoids nearby threats. Risk tolerance controls retreating: Cautious retreats home below 40% health, Steady below 20%, and Fearless never retreats automatically. Companions do not attack players or owned companions.

REQUESTS AND TALENTS

Check in to generate a contextual request. Completing normal requests awards individual companion points and shared pack points. Children receive a safe request pool and bank their talent points until adulthood. Companion points buy talents for that individual adult companion. Talent trees cover Combat, Survival, and Social / Economy.

BREEDING AND CHILDREN

Breeding is opt-in for each supported adult. A female and male of the same species and type must both be At Ease, each have breeding enabled, and have assigned beds in the same fully enclosed room. One 35% attempt can occur per female per night. A successful pregnancy bonds the pair by stable companion identity. Pregnancy reduces movement to 80% and expedition strength to 60%; the Companion and Pack screens show the restriction. Birth waits for the mother to be present, healthy enough, and near safe loaded ground. Children retain their source mod's parent-follow, play, flee, feeding, and growth behavior while gaining basic companion commands and safe requests.

PACK STATUS

Pack status is the home hub for the whole pack. It shows active companions, archived records, shared cargo cache, and pack points. Children appear in the roster but cannot join expeditions.

PACK CART

The Pack Cart is the pack headquarters. Roster shows pack members. Expeditions sends selected adult companions out for work and returns a field report. Routes unlock longer or specialized journeys. Preparation spends pack points once to reduce a journey's danger.

The shared breeding system currently covers first-party foxes, hares, hyenas, wolves, goats, pigs, and sheep, plus compatible adult dogs, cats, and Fox Taming foxes when those mods are installed. Non-breeding variants and unsupported third-party entity domains remain source-owned.
child-command-text: Follow, At Ease, Rest, Return Home, and follow range are available. Combat styles, risk controls, cargo work, talents, and expeditions unlock only after safe adult growth.

expedition-event-smooth-journey-descript: The route stayed quiet and the party kept a steady pace.
expedition-event-good-weather-descriptio: Favorable conditions made the journey easier.
expedition-event-found-bearings-descript: The party corrected its route before losing meaningful time.
expedition-event-heavy-rain-description: Rain obscured the route and made every crossing harder.
expedition-event-difficult-terrain-descr: Rough ground slowed the party and tested its footing.
expedition-event-lost-trail-description: The trail disappeared and the party struggled to find its way.
expedition-event-dangerous-crossing-desc: A dangerous crossing forced the party to take real risks.
expedition-event-pack-tore-description: A carrying pack tore and part of the haul was damaged.
expedition-event-overloaded-cargo-descri: An unusually large find made the journey home slower and harder.
expedition-event-rich-patch-description: The party found a dense patch of useful growth.
expedition-event-untouched-grove-descrip: An undisturbed grove yielded more than the planned route promised.
expedition-event-bee-tree-description: A busy bee tree offered an uncommon foraging opportunity.
expedition-event-excellent-harvest-descr: Careful gathering turned a good find into an excellent harvest.
expedition-event-too-good-to-leave-descr: The party stayed longer to make the most of an exceptional find.
expedition-event-fresh-tracks-descriptio: Fresh signs led the hunters toward productive ground.
expedition-event-large-herd-description: The party found more game than expected.
expedition-event-excellent-quarry-descri: The hunt found unusually valuable quarry.
expedition-event-hard-won-quarry-descrip: The quarry was valuable, but bringing it down came at a cost.
expedition-event-quarry-fought-back-desc: Cornered quarry turned on the hunting party.
expedition-event-long-chase-description: A productive chase carried the party far beyond its planned route.
expedition-event-hidden-cache-descriptio: The party uncovered a concealed store of useful supplies.
expedition-event-forgotten-supplies-desc: Old but useful supplies remained where their owners left them.
expedition-event-intact-container-descri: An intact container survived among the abandoned remains.
expedition-event-abandoned-camp-descript: A deserted camp still held a few worthwhile finds.
expedition-event-difficult-cache-descrip: Valuable supplies were recovered from a hazardous position.
expedition-event-sealed-chamber-descript: The expedition opened a chamber untouched by earlier scavengers.
expedition-event-intact-storeroom-descri: A remarkably intact storeroom held recoverable material.
expedition-event-undisturbed-debris-desc: The party found a rich layer of undisturbed ruin debris.
expedition-event-collapsed-storeroom-des: A storeroom yielded material as its damaged structure gave way.
expedition-event-structural-collapse-des: Part of the ruin collapsed around the expedition.
expedition-event-dangerous-descent-descr: Reaching the deeper ruins required a hazardous descent.
expedition-event-collapsed-passage-descr: A passage collapsed and cut off the expected route home.
expedition-event-lost-underground-descri: The underground route became confused and difficult to retrace.
expedition-event-familiar-scents-descrip: The party paused often to read old scent trails and learn who had passed before them.
expedition-event-rested-under-boughs-des: At midday, the companions found a sheltered place beneath the trees and rested together.
expedition-event-followed-old-trail-desc: A weathered trail carried the party part of the way before fading back into the wild.
expedition-event-shared-watch-descriptio: The companions took turns watching the dark while the rest of the party slept.
expedition-event-sampled-berries-descrip: The foragers inspected unfamiliar berries, tasted nothing doubtful, and marked the patch for another season.
expedition-event-followed-pollinators-de: A line of busy pollinators led the party through a long sweep of flowering ground.
expedition-event-patient-stalk-descripti: The hunters followed a promising trail for hours before deciding the quarry had slipped away cleanly.
expedition-event-false-tracks-descriptio: What looked like a fresh trail proved old and crossed over itself until even the keenest nose lost interest.
expedition-event-sorted-old-scraps-descr: The scavengers picked through a scatter of old scraps, finding stories in them but nothing worth carrying home.
expedition-event-empty-cache-description: The party uncovered a carefully hidden cache that someone else had emptied long ago.
expedition-event-studied-old-marks-descr: The explorers lingered over worn marks in the masonry and argued quietly over what they might mean.
expedition-event-echoes-in-stone-descrip: Every step returned from the dark in strange echoes, but the passages held no further secret that day.
itemdesc-kibble-meat-raw: Raw meat feed for companions. Can be dried in a cooking pot.
itemdesc-kibble-meat-dry:
Dried meat feed for companions.

GUARANTEED ANALYSIS
Crude protein 42%; crude fat 17%; crude fiber 8%; moisture 11%.
FEEDING GUIDE: let the companion negotiate.
INGREDIENTS: meat kibble, grain binder, and one certified squeak of nutritional yeast.
MAY CONTAIN: suspicious bone fragments, unsolicited howling, spontaneous pack formation, and livestock reconsideration.
LEGAL / SAFETY: not intended for human consumption. Bears: yes. Wolf staring at owner: another serving at owner's discretion. Settling during shipping may occur.
Analysis performed by an imaginary clipboard. The clipboard has since joined the pack.
Microscopic fine print: excessive shedding, unsolicited advice from poultry, and renewed interest in the neighbor's cart are not covered by this guarantee.
itemdesc-kibble-plant-raw: Raw vegetable feed for companions. Can be dried in a cooking pot.
itemdesc-kibble-plant-dry:
Dried vegetable feed for companions.

GUARANTEED ANALYSIS
Crude protein 12%; crude fat 5%; crude fiber 18%; moisture 11%.
FEEDING GUIDE: let the companion negotiate.
INGREDIENTS: vegetables, grain binder, and one certified leaf-shaped vitamin.
MAY CONTAIN: stubborn roots, spontaneous garden circles, and opinions about compost.
LEGAL / SAFETY: not intended for human consumption. Bears: also yes. Cabbage: do not challenge it to a staring contest. Settling during shipping may occur.
Analysis performed by an imaginary clipboard. The clipboard has since joined the garden.
Microscopic fine print: the product has never personally met a meadow, despite what the label's marketing department claims.
